attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Follow-up for ongoing concerns regarding delayed speech development and school performance difficulties as patient enters first grade.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for developmental-behavioral pediatrics follow-up one year following initial genetics clinic evaluation for developmental concerns. He presents with ongoing concerns regarding delayed speech development and school performance difficulties as he enters first grade. They mention that he started speaking later than his peers and still struggles to form complete sentences. Teachers have reported difficulties with attention and occasional repetitive behaviors in class. His parents describe him as socially friendly but easily frustrated when routines are changed. The boy has had normal hearing tests and no history of seizures or head trauma.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Fragile X syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Intellectual disability
- Expressive language disorder
- Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
- Generalized anxiety disorder

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tympanostomy tube placement at age 4 years
- Circumcision (neonatal)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Guanfacine extended-release 1 mg oral daily in the morning for attention and hyperarousal
- Sertraline 12.5 mg oral daily for anxiety
- Melatonin 3 mg oral at bedtime for sleep-onset insomnia

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal grandfather: Intellectual disability (suspected undiagnosed Fragile X syndrome)
- Mother: FMR1 gene premutation carrier with history of premature ovarian insufficiency
- Maternal uncle: Learning difficulties and social anxiety

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Student (1st grade).

VITAL SIGNS:
Growth parameters show that his weight and height are within the 50th percentile, but his head circumference is slightly increased.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, he is cooperative but fidgets frequently and avoids sustained eye contact. His face appears long, with a prominent jaw and high-arched palate; his ears are large, and he has hyperextensible joints. Neurological examination is nonfocal, with normal tone and strength in all extremities.

OTHER STUDIES:
Developmental assessment confirms mild intellectual impairment with deficits in expressive language.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-07-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Child Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening anxiety symptoms and increasing academic struggles with peer interactions and self-talk behaviors reported by teachers.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for follow-up regarding concerns evaluated in 2020 for hand flapping and social difficulties, with assessment in 2021 for speech delay and school performance. His teachers report that he is not keeping up with his peers academically and is often found talking to himself during class. His parents also mention that he has been increasingly anxious and has difficulty interacting with other children.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Fragile X syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Intellectual disability
- Expressive language disorder
- Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
- Generalized anxiety disorder

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tympanostomy tube placement at age 4 years
- Circumcision (neonatal)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Guanfacine extended-release 1 mg oral daily in the morning for attention and hyperarousal
- Sertraline 12.5 mg oral daily for anxiety
- Melatonin 3 mg oral at bedtime for sleep-onset insomnia

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
His mother mentions that her brother had similar issues in school and also had large ears, but she is not aware of a formal diagnosis.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Student (1st grade).

VITAL SIGNS:
His height and weight are at the 75th percentile for his age.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the boy has a long face, a prominent forehead, large protruding ears, and an enlarged head circumference. The physical examination is notable for testicular enlargement.
